positions.commentary: The speakers view MSCI as a company they own that levered up its balance sheet substantially over the last couple of years because there have been opportunities to buy shares at a cheap discount.
The speaker describes Berkshire as having a beautiful and crazy balance sheet today, noting opportunities to buy back stock or make acquisitions, though acknowledging it could change in the future.
The speakers praise Apple for doing an amazing job of buying back shares and working down the cash on its balance sheet.
The speakers view Copart as a great example of a long-term mindset where owning the land prevents the lesser from changing the use of the land when a lease is over.
The speaker praises TFI International and Canada's management, noting that Elaine Bedard is making acquisitions left and right and is probably worth 500 million dollars.
The speakers view Amazon's dominance as being because they control the logistics network and have hard assets that are very difficult to replicate.
The speaker argues that waiting for Costco to return to a lower valuation like 32 times earnings is not a valid investment thesis.

The speaker describes buying PayPal at 50 times earnings as one of their biggest mistakes, noting they overpaid on what they thought was a good business which turned out to be not a good business whatsoever.
The speaker implies that buying Meta when it was heavily invested in reality labs was risky and that stocks don't fall randomly.
The speaker suggests that buying Netflix when it was down 60% from the high was a mistake because the thesis was likely broken.
The speaker mentions they bought Charter in 2020 and sold it a loss, but notes it wasn't too bad.
The speakers criticize people who claimed Nvidia was overvalued before its run using PEP multiples for depressed earnings, noting the stock is now up 400%.
Cisco had fake profits during the tech bubble era.
The speaker believes Adobe will continue to grow double digits even 10 years later despite a lower terminal rate forecast.
Microsoft is in everything from gaming to cloud and keeps adding more things.
Google has been around for 30 years and is defying the odds.
The speaker cites Sherwin Williams as a classic example of a market leader that crushed it in the paint industry.
The speakers argue that Danaher's thesis has not changed so much because the management team and founders know how to allocate capital and use culture to improve businesses.
